report.summary: Analyzed chunk 5 of worktree.py, lines 481-570, containing the removal loop with reparse point checks and parent-before-child directory removal.

handoff.purpose: Implement removal loop with reparse point checks and directory removal in reverse order.

symbols.name: _verify_reachable
symbols.note: Called multiple times to check path is still within original tree.

symbols.name: _is_reparse_point
symbols.note: Checks if path is a reparse point (symlink/junction).

symbols.name: WorktreeRemovalRace
symbols.note: Exception raised when race condition detected.

claims.text: A reparse point strictly above ``target`` redirects it wholesale, and unlinking that ancestor would delete a link the manager does not own, so this refuses instead of repairing.
claims.why: The claim refers to behavior of _chain_between and guarded, which are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: os.lstat(root) raises FileNotFoundError if it vanished
claims.why: The code calls os.lstat(root) without a try-except, so it will raise FileNotFoundError if root does not exist.

claims.text: Whatever put `current` on the queue classified it when its parent was enumerated; by now that classification is arbitrarily old, and a live process in the tree has had the whole intervening traversal to invalidate it.
claims.why: The claim refers to classification done elsewhere (not in this chunk).

claims.text: What this one specifically stops, measured: a swap of an ancestor AFTER `current` was queued, which sends the not-a-directory branch below into an os.unlink outside the tree.
claims.why: Claim refers to measured behavior not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: `entries` can be thousands long, and `current` can be renamed aside and a junction renamed into its place between any two iterations
claims.why: Claim about potential race conditions not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: os.unlink resolves the path argument it is given through a reparse point in an intermediate component, so an unlink here that trusts the verification done when `current` was popped deletes FILE CONTENT outside the tree
claims.why: Claim about os.unlink behavior and consequences not verifiable from this chunk.
Claim about syscall count not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: A FRESH lstat, deliberately not entry.stat(): on Windows the DirEntry's stat is served from this scandir's cache (measured), so asking the DirEntry would re-introduce the stale read.
claims.why: Claim about Windows behavior not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: mutation testing shows the suite does NOT go red if it is deleted, and that is not an oversight in the tests -- it is redundant on this platform, measured both ways.
claims.where: HONEST NOTE ON THIS BRANCH comment
claims.why: Claim about mutation testing results not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: A junction is reported as a directory by is_dir(follow_symlinks=False), so it would be queued and then unlinked by the pop-time check; a directory symlink is NOT, so it would fall to _force_unlink, and os.unlink removes a Windows directory symlink without following it (measured: link gone, target intact).
claims.where: HONEST NOTE ON THIS BRANCH comment
claims.why: Claim about platform-specific behavior not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: It is kept because both of those are platform behaviours rather than guarantees, and because it makes the intent explicit at the point of the decision.
claims.where: HONEST NOTE ON THIS BRANCH comment
claims.why: Claim about reason for keeping code not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Cached, and allowed to be: nothing is traversed on the strength of it -- `child` is re-classified when it is popped.
claims.why: Claim about re-classification not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Also cached, also safe: os.unlink removes a link rather than following it, so the worst case is a loud failure.
claims.why: Claim about os.unlink behavior not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Children before parents: a parent is always popped before its children are queued, so its index is lower.
claims.why: The code uses reversed(directories), which processes children first because they are appended later (higher index).

claims.text: RE-VERIFIED PER DIRECTORY. Every entry here was classified when it was POPPED, which for the first one drained is the ENTIRE walk ago, and os.rmdir resolves its path argument through a reparse point in an intermediate component exactly as os.scandir does. An unverified drain therefore lets a junction renamed over an already-drained subdirectory redirect every remaining rmdir out of the tree. Measured, 3/3, end to end through cleanup_worktree: 3000 empty directories removed inside a stand-in primary checkout, reported as success.
claims.why: Claim about measured behavior and cleanup_worktree not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Not repaired by unlinking the link: this directory was emptied by the walk above, so whatever is here now is not what was emptied, and the link is not the manager's to delete. Refuse, and report the tree as partially removed.
claims.why: Claim about ownership and repair not verifiable from this chunk.

observations.what: The chunk contains extensive comments about race conditions and measured behavior, but no tests or external references to verify them.
The code calls _verify_reachable on each child and directory, but the implementation of _verify_reachable is not in this chunk.
The comment claims that mutation testing shows the branch checking _is_reparse_point(child) is redundant on this platform, but the code keeps it for explicitness.
